item.title: Jazz Brunch w/ “Four Peanuts” trio — Sat Nov 28, 11:30 AM — French Broad River Brewery
item.description:
Jazz Brunch is now officially on the schedule for every Saturday here in the taproom! We’re so very excited to introduce our newest free weekly event, open to all ages, family & pet-friendly
If you haven’t experienced Jazz Brunch yet, here’s what you can expect: from the moment the music begins, the taproom fills with that perfect weekend energy… laid-back jazz, fresh brunch plates, great beer, and a room full of people settling in and staying awhile. Friends gather around tables, conversations flow easily, and the rhythm of the music sets the tone for a perfect, easy Saturday. It’s exactly the kind of atmosphere we hoped to create when this idea first came to life!
We’re especially excited to continue working with our house Jazz band, “Four Peanuts”, whose smooth, soulful sound brings everything together. item.title: Holiday Tree Lighting Block Party! — Sat Nov 28, 3:00 PM — The Grove Arcade
item.description:
We’re getting ready for the most wonderful time of the year, and that means the return of the annual Grove Arcade Holiday Tree Lighting Block Party! Join us on Saturday, November 28, for a day of holiday festivities in the heart of downtown Asheville. The celebration kicks off with the Southern Highland Craft Guild Holiday Market at 10AM, followed by an evening of live entertainment, festive drinks, and holiday traditions for the whole family. This year, enjoy holiday cheer with: 🎄 Live performances by @ashevilleballet 🎄 Live music from the Bill Bares Jazz Trio 🎄 Caroling by the @avlgmc 🎄 A visit from Santa Claus, with photo opportunities 🎄 A festive DJ set by @rockthediscosoundsystem , featuring the @captainsofrevelry 🎄 Outdoor pop-up bars on Restaurant Row 🎄 A family-friendly Letters to Santa crafting station 🎄 The @craftguild Holiday Market …and more!
Source: LiveMusicAsheville.com

item.title: 9:15 Contemplative Service — Sun Nov 29, 9:15 AM — *1 Sanctuary
item.description:
At 9:15 AM, we have a 40-45 minute Contemplative Worship Service. This service invites participants into a reflective, more meditative space, and includes silence, beautiful recorded music and videos, and opportunities for sharing. It also features the sermon and theme which will be the focus in the second service at 11:15 AM. This service is not livestreamed., and it include childcare but not a full religious education program. This service will be particularly good if you need quiet in order to hear well or focus, would prefer a little more space around you, or seek a more contemplative communal experience. Between services, at 10 am we will have coffee hour and special programs. Whether you come to the early service or the later service, we encourage you to consider arriving at 10 am for coffee, conversation, and special programs including conversations with the Board, or Minister & lay-led justice or adult education offerings.
Source: Unitarian Universalist Congregation of Ashevi

item.title: Fiber Friends — Sat Dec 5, 10:00 AM — 23 Ed Parlor
item.description:
UU Asheville Fiber Friends is a group of crafters who do handwork on personal projects and for the community. Mainly knitters and crocheters, we create warm items for donation to local charities (serving children, youth, and adults) and make a variety of cotton cloths given to Meals on Wheels for their “Santa for seniors” packages each December. A limited supply of yarn and tools (needles and hooks) are also available.
Join us the first Saturday of each month in the parlor of 23 Edwin, from 10 AM until about 12 noon. For more information or to be added to the monthly email reminder list, contact Mara Sprain.
Source: Unitarian Universalist Congregation of Asheville

That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. item.title: Fun & easy way to play more tennis (please read event description for details) — Thu Dec 17, 7:00 PM
item.description:
PlayYourCourt Asheville Tennis We’re still working to get more people into these Meetups, but our goal is to give PlayYourCourt members a few social tennis outings each week in addition to your practice sessions and Challenge League matches.
These Meetups are co-ed, super laid back, and all skill levels are welcome. Post your skill level and a suggested court in the comments section so we can round up as many players as we can for some tennis fun!
Also, if you’re looking to meet new practice partners or play some matches and you aren’t already in the PlayYourCourt Community, you can go here to see what we’re all about and sign up:
https://www.playyourcourt.com/tennis-community/asheville-nc/meetup/
If you love tennis, we’d love to have you! Be sure and watch the quick video that explains how everything works.
Happy hitting!
- Scott
Source: PlayYourCourt Asheville Tennis

item.title: Buncombe County Parks Update - Open and Closed Parks — Fri Jan 29
item.description: Email: parks@buncombecounty.orgPhone: (828) 250-4260Notice - Description: Information about Open and Closed ParksMany Buncombe County Parks were impacted by Hurricane Helene. While we are working diligently reopen parks as quickly as we can, some parks continue to remain closed. Please see the list below for which parks are open and which parks continue to be closed for safety reasons.OPEN Parks: Lake Julian Park (please note, some disc golf holes remain closed), Hominy Valley Park, Collier Cove Nature Preserve, North Buncombe Fields, Cane Creek Playground, Buncombe County Sports Park, Corcoran Paige River Park, Bent Creek River Park, Ledges Whitewater Park, and Hominy Creek River Park. If people choose to recreate on the river, we strongly encourage them to be aware of changes on streambanks and in the riverbed and the potential for unknown debris from Helene.CLOSED Parks: Charles D.
